text: If I'd known, I would've stayed.

I have been sailing for forty years, and my worst day at sea was my own fault. We left the marina on a beautiful morning, and I did not check the forecast. In the afternoon, the wind changed, and a big gust hit us. We almost capsized. If I had checked the forecast, we would not have left that day. And if my friend Tom had not taken the helm, I think we would have hit the rocks. I should have reduced the sail much earlier, and I should have listened to the old fishermen at the bar. They told me the sky looked wrong. We got back in one piece, but I learned my lesson. Now I check the forecast twice.

People think the dangerous moment at sea is the storm. For me, it was a quiet night with no wind at all. Our engine stopped, and the boat started to drift towards the coast. I did not panic, but I was very close. Luckily, I had a radio, and the coast guard arrived in twenty minutes. If I had not had that radio, we would have run aground on the rocks. Honestly, I should have checked the engine before we left. It was making a strange noise all week. The young sailors at my club sometimes say I am too careful. Maybe. But I have never been reckless since that night.
If we had checked the forecast, we would not have left.
If Tom had not taken the helm, we would have hit the rocks.
I should have worn a lifejacket.
If I had known, I would have stayed at the marina.
It was a close call. We almost hit the rocks.
We got back to the marina in one piece.
